narrative:
The model predicts you have a 19% chance of failing your final year. While this is not a high probability, it is enough for the school to require you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The prediction that you might fail is driven mainly by three aspects of your situation. The most influential factor is that you have had no past class failures. Surprisingly, this actually pushes the model toward expecting you to fail. Among students who passed, having zero previous failures is the norm, but in your specific combination of circumstances the model sees the absence of any prior setbacks as a warning sign rather than a strength. 

The second most important influence is your strong desire to pursue higher education. This works in your favor and pulls the prediction toward passing, because every student who passed also expressed this ambition.

The third factor is how often you go out with friends. Your medium level of socializing slightly increases the chance of failing. Most students who passed went out at a similar or lower rate, so this moderate social time is working against you in the model’s eyes.

To improve, focus on turning your clear ambition for higher education into concrete daily study habits. Reducing time spent going out, even by a small amount, and replacing it with structured revision could lower your risk considerably. Taking the remedial courses seriously will also help close any gaps before the final exams.
